card: Adds an auto_outbound_mode to the functional test framework and uses it to test outbound connection management logic. Currently, functional tests typically establish connections directly from the test runner, leaving the node's autonomous connection decisions poorly covered. The change allows nodes to make addrman-driven outbound connections redirected via a local SOCKS5 proxy, providing test coverage for stale-tip extra connections (#11560), periodic block-relay connections (#19858), and network diversification (#27213).
evidence: PR description: 'The second commit uses it to add functional test coverage for the following features of outbound connection management: extra full outbound connections due to a stale tip (#11560), periodic block-relay-only connections (#19858), full outbound connection management with respect to networks (#27213)'

Commit message for 6bcb43b4cd: 'This new option allows tests to make use of automatic outbound connections (made from addrman). A SOCKS5 proxy is used to redirect the connection, by default to a P2PInterface.'
problem: P2P logic where bitcoind autonomously decides when and how to make outbound connections (such as reacting to stale chain tips, scheduling periodic block-relay connections, or diversifying peers across networks) lacked realistic functional test coverage because standard functional tests rely on the test runner actively initiating connections to the node.
scope_notes: Extracts reusable SOCKS5 redirection machinery from `p2p_private_broadcast.py` into test framework helpers before adding the new test suite.
summary: This pull request integrates an `auto_outbound_mode` helper into the functional test framework and adds a new test exercising automatic outbound connection logic. It enables the node under test to autonomously initiate outbound connections to addrman entries redirected via an internal SOCKS5 proxy to test peers or other nodes, rather than relying on test-initiated outbound connections. The PR also uses this framework to add test coverage for stale-tip extra outbound connections, periodic block-relay-only connections, and network-diversified outbound connection management.
